what_it_does: Cyber-physical systems (CPS) — think industrial robots, self-driving cars, or power grids — rely on sensors feeding real-time data to control software that monitors for anomalies. An attacker who can manipulate those sensor readings can cause the system to behave dangerously, but modern CPS also run anomaly detectors that will raise an alarm if the sensor values look suspicious. This paper studies how an attacker with very little knowledge of the system (a "black-box" scenario — they cannot see the detector's internals and can only observe whether it does or does not raise an alarm) could learn the detector's behavior through careful probing and then craft sensor-reading sequences that look plausible enough to slip past the detector. The key challenge is learning enough about the detector without asking it so many questions that the probing itself triggers an alarm, so the method uses a budget-aware active learning strategy that extracts a model of the detector incrementally and conservatively.
